newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice Dept. clears CIA nominee Lake.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice Dept. clears CIA nominee Lake.

text.p: The Justice Department on Friday cleared former White House National Security Adviser Anthony Lake of criminal wrongdoing in his stock dealings and allegations he lied to Congress about Bosnia arms policy.

But Lake, President Clinton's nominee to head the Central Intelligence Agency, did enter into a civil settlement with the Justice Department over his failure to sell four energy stocks. The proposed settlement agreement called for him to pay civil penalties of $5,000.
A Justice Department spokesman said it had ended its criminal investigation into the stock sales.

On the Bosnia arms sales, the Justice Department said it determined "there is no basis for any criminal charges" against Lake. House Republicans alleged he lied to Congress about the shipment of Iranian arms to Bosnia.
The two actions cleared the way for the Senate Intelligence Committee to hold hearings late in February on Clinton's nomination of Lake to head the CIA.
Clinton's choices of Lake and of former White House aide Alexis Herman as labour secretary have been the most controversial of the Cabinet nominations he has sent to the Republican-controlled Senate.
